newsitem.title: USA: Clinton report on electronic commerce due July 1.
newsitem.headline: Clinton report on electronic commerce due July 1.

text.p: The Clinton administration will release on July 1 a statement of goals and principles intended to foster electronic commerce, administration officials said on Monday.
The report concludes that the Internet could provide a huge boost to the U.S. economy if the federal government pursues market-oriented policies in cyberspace, officials said.
Based on a draft released by the White House in December, the final report will include recommendations on nine issues ranging from taxation and customs to privacy and security.
In addition, the final report will also include specific actions and achievements that the administration plans to pursue, officials said.
For example, the United States may push to have the Internet declared a duty-free zone by the World Trade Organization.
Internet-specific taxes and tariffs should be avoided to foster the growth of online trade, officials said.
On the issue of privacy, companies should be encouraged to disclose what will be done with information gathered from consumers.
